description:
## Finding
\`pkix-lint/src/cabf_tls_br.rs:217-267\`. Lint \`cabf.br.tls.rsa.min_key_size\`:
- Doc title (L195): \"RSA certificates ... must have a modulus of at least 2048 bits.\"
- Citation: CA/B Forum TLS BR §6.1.5.
- Implementation: checks DER INTEGER byte length \`>= 256\`. The doc explains that a 2047-bit modulus also encodes as 256 bytes (no leading 0x00 because high bit of first byte is 0).
- \"This matches zlint's floor-byte comparison behavior: 2047-bit keys with 256 bytes pass this check.\"

## Why P2
- CA/B Forum BR §6.1.5 says \"at least 2048 bits.\" 2047 ≠ 2048; accepting 2047-bit keys is non-conformant.
- zlint behavior is not the spec oracle. AGENTS.md test-integrity rule says external oracles must be the spec or independent reference implementations, not implementations under audit.
- The lint doc title and citation imply spec-conformance but the check is intentionally relaxed below spec.

## Fix
Two coherent options:
1. Tighten the check to actually require 2048 bits: count high-bit position of the modulus first byte and require \`bit_len >= 2048\`. The pkix-path \`rsa_public_key_bits\` helper already does this byte_len * 8 calculation; reuse that pattern.
2. Document the leniency as a deliberate lint relaxation (and rename the lint id, e.g., \`cabf.br.tls.rsa.min_key_size_lenient\`) so callers wanting strict conformance can layer a separate lint on top.

Option 1 is closer to the citation. Option 2 preserves zlint compatibility.

## Scope reference
\`pkix-lint/src/cabf_tls_br.rs:195-267\`.
title: P2: RsaMinKeySizeLint accepts 2047-bit RSA keys despite "2048-bit minimum" claim
